summary: Credo sells the active electrical cables, SerDes and optical DSPs that connect AI servers, and it is growing fast and profitably: fiscal Q1 2027 revenue rose 115% to $479M with a 48% non-GAAP operating margin, and it guided Q2 to $525-535M. The stock has fallen about 46% from its $308.67 high after a roughly 20% post-earnings drop on GAAP gross-margin compression from the DustPhotonics deal, leaving it at about 26x fiscal 2027 and 17x fiscal 2028 consensus EPS. Our $150-270 range (mid $210) puts it inside fair value but with about 27% upside to the mid-point, so we lean Overweight. The main risks are heavy customer concentration (top three about 74% of revenue) and steady insider selling.

valuation.method: (a) Peers: Astera Labs traded ~115x forward earnings in July; Credo at ~26x FY27 is much cheaper for similar AI-connectivity growth. (b) Earnings power: FY28 consensus EPS $9.69 at 20-30x, discounted one year at 10%, gives ~$176-264; a bear case of 18x on a 15% lower EPS lands near $150. (c) Analyst targets: average $279 (20 analysts, 19 Buy/Strong Buy), high $310 (Stifel, JPMorgan). Fair range $150-270, mid $210.
valuation.note: Marvell and Broadcom current multiples were not found in sources read this run. Forward multiples use consensus quoted by 24/7 Wall St and StockAnalysis.
